bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷六十九 南平世家第九: 高季興
title.raw: 卷六十九 南平世家第九: 高季興 Volume 69: Hereditary House of Nanping

sentences.zh: 高季興，字貽孫，陜州硤石人也。

translations.literal: Gao Jixing, courtesy name Yisun, was a man of Xiaashi in Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jixing, whose courtesy name was Yisun, came from Xiaashi in Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本名季昌，避後唐獻祖廟諱，更名季興。

translations.literal: His original name was Jichang; to avoid the taboo of the temple name of Later Tang's founding ancestor, he was renamed Jixing.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally been named Jichang, but to avoid the taboo on the temple name of Later Tang's founding ancestor, he took the name Jixing.

sentences.zh: 季興少為汴州富人李讓家僮。

translations.literal: In his youth Jixing was a household slave in the home of Li Rang, a wealthy man of Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man, Jixing served as a household slave in the home of Li Rang, a wealthy man of Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖初鎮宣武，讓以入貲得幸，養為子，易其姓名曰朱友讓。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor of Liang first governed Xuanyi, Rang gained favor by contributing wealth, was adopted as a son, and his name was changed to Zhu Yourang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor of Liang first took charge of Xuanyi, Rang won his favor by paying a large contribution and was adopted as a son; his name was then changed to Zhu Yourang.

sentences.zh: 季興以友讓故得進見，太祖奇其材，命友讓以子畜之，因冒姓朱氏，補制勝軍使，遷毅勇指揮使。

translations.literal: Jixing was able to gain an audience because of Yourang; the Founding Emperor was struck by his talent, ordered Yourang to rear him as a son, and he therefore falsely took the surname Zhu; he was appointed military commissioner of the Victorious Army and was transferred to commander of the Resolute and Brave Command.
translations.idiomatic: Through Yourang, Jixing obtained an audience with the emperor, who was impressed by his ability and told Yourang to raise him as a son. He thereupon took the Zhu surname for a time, was appointed commissioner of the Victorious Army, and later became commander of the Resolute and Brave Command.

sentences.zh: 天復二年，梁兵攻鳳翔，李茂貞堅壁不出，太祖議欲收軍還河中，季興獨進曰：「天下豪傑窺此舉者一歲矣，今岐人已憊，破在旦夕，而大王之所慮者，閉壁以老我師，此可以誘致之也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu, Liang troops attacked Fengxiang; Li Maozhen held his walls and would not come out; the Founding Emperor discussed withdrawing the army back to Hezhong; Jixing alone advanced and said: "For a year now the heroes of the realm have been watching this campaign; today the men of Qi are exhausted and defeat is imminent; what Your Highness fears is that they will shut their walls to wear down our army—this can be lured out."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu, Liang forces besieged Fengxiang while Li Maozhen held the walls and refused to give battle. The Founding Emperor considered withdrawing to Hezhong, but Jixing alone stepped forward and said, "For a year the empire's strongmen have watched this campaign. The Qi forces are worn out now and will fall any day. What worries you, my lord, is their strategy of shutting the gates to exhaust our army—that is something we can lure them out of."

sentences.zh: 」太祖壯其言，命季興募勇敢士，得騎士馬景，季興授以計，引見太祖。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was impressed by his words, ordered Jixing to recruit brave men, obtained the cavalryman Ma Jing, Jixing gave him the plan, and introduced him to the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was struck by his counsel and told Jixing to recruit daring men. Jixing found the cavalryman Ma Jing, taught him the stratagem, and presented him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 景曰：「此行無還理，願錄其後嗣。

translations.literal: Jing said: "On this mission there is no prospect of return; I ask that my descendants be recorded."
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "There is no coming back from this mission. I ask that my descendants be provided for."

sentences.zh: 」太祖惻然止之，景固請，乃行。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, moved with pity, tried to stop him; Jing firmly requested to go, and then set out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved, tried to dissuade him, but Jing insisted and set out.

sentences.zh: 景以數騎馳叩城門告曰：「梁兵將東，前鋒去矣。

translations.literal: Jing with several horsemen galloped to knock on the city gate and announced: "The Liang army is about to march east; the vanguard has already gone."
translations.idiomatic: Riding with a few horsemen, Jing galloped to the gate and shouted that the Liang army was withdrawing eastward and that the vanguard had already departed.

sentences.zh: 」岐人以為然，開門出追梁軍，梁兵隨景後以進，殺其九千餘人，景死之。

translations.literal: The men of Qi believed it, opened the gate and came out to pursue the Liang army; Liang troops followed behind Jing and advanced, killing more than nine thousand of them; Jing died in the action.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders believed him, opened the gates, and rushed out in pursuit. Liang troops followed close behind Jing and cut down more than nine thousand men; Jing himself was killed in the fight.

sentences.zh: 茂貞後與梁和，昭宗出，贈景官，謚曰忠壯。

translations.literal: Later Maozhen made peace with Liang; when Emperor Zhaozong came out, he conferred posthumous office on Jing and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen later made peace with Liang. When Emperor Zhaozong was released, he granted Jing a posthumous office and the posthumous title Loyal and Stalwart.

sentences.zh: 季興由是知名。

translations.literal: Jixing thereby became well known.
translations.idiomatic: From this Jixing won renown.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜宋州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed prefect of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed prefect of Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從破青州，徙潁州防禦使，復姓高氏。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Qing Prefecture, was transferred to defender of Ying Prefecture, and resumed the surname Gao.
translations.idiomatic: After taking part in the conquest of Qing Prefecture, he was transferred to defender of Ying Prefecture and restored the Gao surname.

sentences.zh: 當唐之末，襄州趙匡凝襲破雷彥恭於荊南，以其弟匡明為留後。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, Zhao Kuangning of Xiang Prefecture made a surprise attack and defeated Lei Yangong in Jingnan, and appointed his younger brother Kuangming as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Tang, Zhao Kuangning of Xiang Prefecture surprised and defeated Lei Yangong in Jingnan, then installed his younger brother Kuangming as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 梁兵攻破襄州，匡凝奔於吳，匡明奔於蜀，乃以季興為荊南節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: Liang troops captured Xiang Prefecture; Kuangning fled to Wu and Kuangming fled to Shu; Jixing was then made acting military governor and surveillance commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang forces took Xiang Prefecture, Kuangning fled to Wu and Kuangming to Shu. Jixing was then appointed acting military governor and surveillance commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 開平元年，拜季興節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiping he was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiping he was formally appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 二年，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was given the additional title of co-acting associate minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was also made co-acting associate minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度十州，當唐之末，為諸道所侵，季興始至，江陵一城而已，兵火之後，井邑雕零。

translations.literal: The ten prefectures of the Jingnan command had, at the end of Tang, been encroached upon by the various circuits; when Jixing first arrived, only the single city of Jiangling remained; after the fires of war, towns and hamlets lay in ruins.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingnan command comprised ten prefectures, but by the end of Tang neighboring circuits had stripped them away. When Jixing first took office, only Jiangling itself was left; after years of war, towns and villages lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 季興招緝綏撫，人士歸之，乃以倪可福、鮑唐為將帥，梁震、司空熏、王保義等為賓客。

translations.literal: Jixing gathered, soothed, and comforted the people; men of talent came to him; he then made Ni Kefu and Bao Tang his generals, and Liang Zhen, Sikong Xun, Wang Baoyi, and others his retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing recruited refugees, eased their hardships, and won people back to the region. He appointed Ni Kefu and Bao Tang as his commanders and took Liang Zhen, Sikong Xun, Wang Baoyi, and others as his advisers.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，季興見梁日以衰弱，乃謀阻兵自固，治城隍，設樓櫓。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor died, Jixing saw that Liang grew weaker day by day; he then plotted to hold troops and secure himself, repaired the moat and walls, and set up watchtowers.
translations.idiomatic: After the Founding Emperor's death, Jixing watched Liang weaken day by day and set about strengthening his own position: he repaired the city walls and moats and built watchtowers.

sentences.zh: 以兵攻歸、峽，為蜀將王宗壽所敗。

translations.literal: He sent troops to attack Gui and Xia, and was defeated by the Shu general Wang Zongshou.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Gui and Xia Prefectures but was defeated by the Shu general Wang Zongshou.

sentences.zh: 又發兵聲言助梁擊晉，以侵襄州，為孔所敗，乃絕貢賦累年。

translations.literal: He again raised troops, claiming publicly to help Liang attack Jin, in order to invade Xiang Prefecture; he was defeated by Kong, and then cut off tribute and taxes for many years.
translations.idiomatic: He raised troops again, publicly claiming to aid Liang against Jin while actually moving against Xiang Prefecture. Kong Xun defeated him, and he then withheld tribute for many years.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝優容之，封季興渤海王，賜以袞冕劍佩。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor of Liang treated him leniently, enfeoffed Jixing as Prince of Bohai, and bestowed on him imperial robes, sword, and belt ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor of Liang indulged him, enfeoffed him as Prince of Bohai, and granted him imperial robes, sword, and belt ornaments.

sentences.zh: 貞明三年，始復修貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming he at last resumed sending tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenming he finally resumed tribute payments.

sentences.zh: 梁亡，唐莊宗入洛，下詔慰諭季興，司空薰等皆勸季興入朝京師，梁震以為不可，曰：「梁、唐世為仇敵，夾河血戰垂二十年，今主上新滅梁，而大王梁室故臣，握強兵，居重鎮，以身入朝，行為虜爾。

translations.literal: When Liang perished, Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang entered Luoyang and issued an edict to comfort and instruct Jixing; Sikong Xun and others all urged Jixing to go to court in the capital; Liang Zhen thought it inadvisable and said: "Liang and Tang have been enemies for generations; for nearly twenty years they fought bloody battles along the Yellow River; now the ruler has newly destroyed Liang, while Your Highness is a former minister of the Liang house, holding strong troops and occupying a key post—if you go to court in person, you will in effect become a captive."
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell, Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang entered Luoyang and sent an edict of reassurance to Jixing. Sikong Xun and others urged him to attend court in the capital, but Liang Zhen objected: "Liang and Tang were hereditary foes who fought bloody battles along the Yellow River for nearly twenty years. Your new sovereign has just destroyed Liang. You are a former Liang minister who still commands a strong army and holds a strategic post. If you go to court in person, you will walk straight into captivity."

sentences.zh: 」季興不聽，留其二子，以騎士三百為衛，朝於洛陽。

translations.literal: Jixing would not listen; he left his two sons behind, took three hundred cavalrymen as escort, and went to court in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing would not listen. He left his two sons behind, took three hundred horsemen as an escort, and went to court in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 莊宗果欲留之，郭崇韜諫曰：「唐新滅梁得天下，方以大信示人，今四方諸侯相繼入貢，不過遣子弟將吏，而季興以身述職，為諸侯率，宜加恩禮，以諷動來者。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong indeed wished to detain him; Guo Chongtao remonstrated and said: "Tang has newly destroyed Liang and gained the realm; it is just now showing great trust to the people; the feudatories of the four quarters are coming in tribute one after another, but none more than sending sons, younger brothers, generals, and officials—yet Jixing has come in person to report his duties, taking the lead among the feudatories; he should be treated with added favor and ceremony to encourage those who will come."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong did intend to detain him, but Guo Chongtao remonstrated: "Tang has just overthrown Liang and won the realm. We are trying to show the world that we govern by trust. The regional lords are sending tribute one after another, but only through sons, officers, or deputies. Jixing has come in person to report for duty and has set an example for them all. We should honor him generously to encourage others to follow."

sentences.zh: 而反縻之，示天下以不廣，且絕四方內向之意，不可。

translations.literal: Yet if we instead hold him captive, we show the realm a lack of magnanimity and cut off the inclination of the four quarters to turn inward—this cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: If we detain him instead, we will show the world that we lack magnanimity and cut off the willingness of the regions to submit. That must not be done."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗乃止，厚禮而遣之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong then stopped, treated him generously, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong relented, treated him with great courtesy, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嘗問季興曰：「吾已滅梁，欲征吳、蜀，何者為先？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong once asked Jixing: "I have already destroyed Liang and wish to campaign against Wu and Shu—which should come first?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong once asked Jixing, "I have destroyed Liang and now mean to campaign against Wu and Shu. Which should I strike first?"

sentences.zh: 」季興曰：「宜先蜀，臣請以本道兵先進。

translations.literal: Jixing said: "Shu should come first; your servant asks to advance first with the troops of this circuit."
translations.idiomatic: Jixing replied, "Shu should come first. I ask leave to advance ahead with the forces of my own circuit."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗大悅，以手拊其背，季興因命工繡其手跡於衣，歸以為榮耀。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was greatly pleased and clapped him on the back with his hand; Jixing thereupon ordered craftsmen to embroider the imprint of that hand on his robe, and on returning regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was delighted and clapped him on the back. Jixing had artisans embroider the imprint of the emperor's hand on his robe and regarded it as a mark of glory when he returned home.

sentences.zh: 季興已去，莊宗心悔遣之，密詔襄州劉訓圖之。

translations.literal: After Jixing had gone, Zhuangzong regretted in his heart having sent him away and secretly ordered Liu Xun of Xiang Prefecture to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jixing had left, Zhuangzong regretted letting him go and secretly ordered Liu Xun of Xiang Prefecture to seize him.

sentences.zh: 季興行至襄州，心動，夜斬關而出。

translations.literal: When Jixing reached Xiang Prefecture his heart was stirred; in the night he cut through the pass and went out.
translations.idiomatic: When Jixing reached Xiang Prefecture he sensed danger, broke through the pass by night, and fled.

sentences.zh: 已去，而詔書夜至。

translations.literal: He had already gone when the edict arrived that night.
translations.idiomatic: He was already gone when the arrest edict arrived that same night.

sentences.zh: 季興歸而謂梁震曰：「不聽子言，幾不免。

translations.literal: On returning, Jixing said to Liang Zhen: "Had I not listened to your words, I would barely have escaped."
translations.idiomatic: After he returned, Jixing told Liang Zhen, "If I had not taken your advice, I would barely have escaped with my life."

sentences.zh: 」因曰：「吾行有二失；

translations.literal: He then said: "On this journey I made two mistakes."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "That journey taught me two mistakes."

sentences.zh: 來朝一失，放還一失。

translations.literal: Coming to court was one mistake; letting me go was another.
translations.idiomatic: Coming to court was one mistake on my part; letting me leave was one on his."

sentences.zh: 且主上百戰以取河南，對功臣誇手抄《春秋》；

translations.literal: Moreover the ruler, after a hundred battles to take the lands south of the Yellow River, boasted to his meritorious ministers that he had copied the Spring and Autumn Annals by hand;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after a hundred battles to win the Central Plains, the emperor boasted to his meritorious ministers that he had copied the Spring and Autumn Annals by hand;

sentences.zh: 又曰：『我於手指上得天下。

translations.literal: and again said: "I gained the realm on my fingertips."
translations.idiomatic: and also said, "I won the realm on my fingertips."

sentences.zh: 』其自矜伐如此。

translations.literal: Such was the way he vaunted himself.
translations.idiomatic: That is how vain and boastful he is.

sentences.zh: 而荒於遊畋，政事多廢，吾可無慮矣。

translations.literal: Yet he is dissolute in hunting and excursions, and government affairs are largely neglected—I need have no worries."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he neglects government for hunting and sport. I have nothing left to fear from him."

sentences.zh: 」同光三年，封南平王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌已破蜀，得蜀金帛四十餘萬，自峽而下，而莊宗之難作。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Jiji had already defeated Shu and obtained more than four hundred thousand strings of Shu gold and silk, and was coming down from the gorges when Zhuangzong's calamity broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Jiji had conquered Shu and was bringing more than four hundred thousand strings' worth of Shu gold and silk down through the gorges when the crisis at Zhuangzong's court erupted.

sentences.zh: 季興聞京師有變，乃悉邀留蜀物，而殺其使者韓珙等十餘人。

translations.literal: When Jixing heard that there was turmoil in the capital, he detained all the Shu goods and killed more than ten of its envoys, including Han Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of turmoil in the capital, Jixing seized the entire Shu convoy and killed more than ten of its envoys, including Han Gong.

sentences.zh: 初，唐兵伐蜀，季興請以本道兵自取夔、忠、萬、歸、峽等州，乃以季興為峽路東南面招討使，而季興未嘗出兵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Tang troops campaigned against Shu, Jixing asked to take Qian, Zhong, Wan, Gui, Xia, and other prefectures himself with the troops of his circuit; he was then made eastern-southern campaign commissioner of the Gorges Route, yet Jixing never once sent out troops.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Tang forces invaded Shu, Jixing had asked to seize Qian, Zhong, Wan, Gui, Xia, and the other prefectures with his own troops. He was appointed eastern-southern campaign commissioner of the Gorges Route, but never actually marched.

sentences.zh: 魏王已破蜀，而明宗入立，季興因請夔、忠等州為屬郡，唐大臣以為季興請自取之，而兵出無功，不與。

translations.literal: After the Prince of Wei had defeated Shu and Emperor Mingzong had taken the throne, Jixing thereupon asked that Qian, Zhong, and other prefectures be made his subordinate commanderies; Tang ministers held that Jixing had asked to take them himself yet had sent out troops without success, and would not grant them.
translations.idiomatic: After the Prince of Wei conquered Shu and Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Jixing asked that Qian, Zhong, and the other prefectures be annexed to his domain. Tang ministers argued that he had promised to take them himself yet had never contributed troops, and refused.

sentences.zh: 季興屢請，雖不得已而與之，而唐猶自除刺史，季興拒而不納。

translations.literal: Jixing repeatedly requested them; although they were granted him against their will, Tang still appointed the prefects itself, and Jixing refused and would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing pressed the request repeatedly. The court reluctantly granted the prefectures but still appointed its own prefects. Jixing refused to accept them.

sentences.zh: 明宗乃以襄州劉訓為招討使，攻之，不克，而唐別將西方鄴克其夔、忠、萬三州，季興遂以荊、歸、峽三州臣於吳，吳冊季興秦王。

translations.literal: Mingzong then made Liu Xun of Xiang Prefecture campaign commissioner and attacked him, but could not overcome him; meanwhile a separate Tang general, Xi Fangye, captured his three prefectures of Qian, Zhong, and Wan; Jixing thereupon submitted the three prefectures of Jing, Gui, and Xia to Wu, and Wu enfeoffed Jixing as King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong appointed Liu Xun of Xiang Prefecture as campaign commissioner and attacked him without success. Meanwhile the Tang general Xi Fangye seized Qian, Zhong, and Wan. Jixing then submitted Jing, Gui, and Xia to Wu, and Wu enfeoffed him as King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 天成三年冬卒，年七十一，謚曰武信。

translations.literal: He died in the winter of the third year of Tiancheng, aged seventy-one; his posthumous title was Martial and Trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the third year of Tiancheng at the age of seventy-one. His posthumous title was Martial and Trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 季興子九人，長子從誨立。

translations.literal: Jixing had nine sons; his eldest son Conghui succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing had nine sons. His eldest son Conghui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 從誨為人明敏，多權詐。

translations.literal: Conghui as a man was sharp and clever, and full of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Conghui was clever and quick-witted, and skilled in deceit.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖遣翰林學士陶穀為從誨生辰國信使，從誨宴穀望沙樓，大陳戰艦於樓下，謂穀曰：「吳、蜀不賓久矣，願修武備，習水戰，以待師期。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Jin sent Hanlin academician Tao Gu as birthday envoy to Conghui; Conghui entertained Gu at the Wangsha Tower and arrayed many warships below the tower, saying to Gu: "Wu and Shu have long refused submission; I wish to repair armaments, practice naval warfare, and await the day of the imperial army."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Jin sent the Hanlin academician Tao Gu as birthday envoy to Conghui. Conghui entertained him at the Wangsha Tower with a great display of warships below and said, "Wu and Shu have long withheld submission. I mean to strengthen my defenses, train for naval warfare, and await the day when your armies march."

sentences.zh: 」穀還，具道其語，晉高祖大喜，復遣使賜以甲馬百匹。

translations.literal: When Gu returned he reported his words in full; Emperor Gaozu of Jin was greatly pleased and again sent envoys to bestow a hundred suits of armor and horses.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Gu repeated the speech in full. Gaozu was delighted and sent another envoy with a gift of a hundred suits of armor and horses.

sentences.zh: 襄州安從進反，結從誨為援，從誨外為拒絕，陰與之通。

translations.literal: An Congjin of Xiang Prefecture rebelled and sought Conghui as an ally; Conghui outwardly refused but secretly communicated with him.
translations.idiomatic: When An Congjin of Xiang Prefecture rebelled, he sought Conghui as an ally. Conghui publicly refused but secretly aided him.

sentences.zh: 晉師致討，從誨遣將李端以舟師為應，從進誅，從誨求郢州為屬郡，高祖不許。

translations.literal: Jin troops came to punish him; Conghui sent the general Li Duan with a naval force in support; Congjin was executed; Conghui asked that Ying Prefecture be made a subordinate commandery, and Gaozu would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin forces moved against An Congjin, Conghui sent the general Li Duan with a fleet in support. After Congjin was executed, Conghui asked that Ying Prefecture be annexed to his domain, but Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 契丹滅晉，漢高祖起太原，從誨遣人間道奉表勸進，且言漢得天下，願乞郢州為屬，漢高祖陽諾之。

translations.literal: When the Khitans destroyed Jin, Emperor Gaozu of Han rose at Taiyuan; Conghui sent men by secret routes with memorials urging him to take the throne, and also said that if Han gained the realm he wished to beg Ying Prefecture as a dependency; Emperor Gaozu of Han pretended to agree.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans destroyed Jin, Emperor Gaozu of Han rose at Taiyuan. Conghui sent envoys by secret routes urging him to take the throne and promising that if Han won the realm, he would seek Ying Prefecture as a dependency. Gaozu pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 高祖入汴，從誨遣使朝貢，因求郢州，高祖不與。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Bian, Conghui sent envoys with tribute and again asked for Ying Prefecture; Gaozu would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Bian, Conghui sent tribute envoys and again asked for Ying Prefecture. Gaozu again refused.

sentences.zh: 從誨怒，發兵攻郢州，為刺史尹實所敗。

translations.literal: Conghui was angry, raised troops to attack Ying Prefecture, and was defeated by the prefect Yin Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Conghui attacked Ying Prefecture and was defeated by its prefect Yin Shi.

sentences.zh: 漢遣國子祭酒田敏使於楚，假道荊南，從誨問敏中國虛實，以為契丹之後，兵食皆殫，意欲以誚敏，敏為言：「杜重威悉以晉戈甲降虜，虜置之鎮州，未嘗以北，而晉兵皆漢有也。

translations.literal: Han sent Guozi libationer Tian Min as envoy to Chu, passing through Jingnan by courtesy; Conghui asked Min about the strength and weakness of the central state, believing that after the Khitans troops and provisions were exhausted, intending to mock Min; Min replied: "Du Chongwei surrendered all Jin arms and armor to the invaders; the invaders placed them at Zhen Prefecture and have never brought them north, while the Jin troops are all in Han's possession."
translations.idiomatic: Han sent the Guozi libationer Tian Min as envoy to Chu, traveling through Jingnan. Conghui asked about the central state's strength, assuming that after the Khitan invasion its armies and supplies were exhausted, and meant to mock him. Min replied, "Du Chongwei surrendered all Jin arms and armor to the invaders. The Khitans stored them at Zhen Prefecture and have never brought them north, while the Jin soldiers themselves are now Han's."

sentences.zh: 」從誨不悅。

translations.literal: Conghui was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Conghui was displeased.

sentences.zh: 敏以印本《五經》遺從誨，從誨謝曰：「予之所識，不過《孝經》十八章爾。

translations.literal: Min presented Conghui with printed copies of the Five Classics; Conghui declined and said: "What I know is no more than the eighteen chapters of the Classic of Filial Piety."
translations.idiomatic: Min presented printed copies of the Five Classics. Conghui declined, saying, "All I know are the eighteen chapters of the Classic of Filial Piety."

sentences.zh: 」敏曰：「至德要道，於此足矣。

translations.literal: Min said: "The utmost virtue and essential Way are fully contained in that."
translations.idiomatic: Min said, "The utmost virtue and the essential Way are fully contained in that."

sentences.zh: 」敏因誦《諸侯章》曰：「在上不驕，高而不危，制節謹度，滿而不溢。

translations.literal: Min then recited the chapter on feudal lords: "Not arrogant when above others, lofty yet not endangered, restraining oneself and observing measure, full yet not overflowing."
translations.idiomatic: Min then recited the chapter on feudal lords: "Not arrogant when above others, lofty yet not endangered, restraining oneself and observing measure, full yet not overflowing."

sentences.zh: 」從誨以為譏己，即以大卮罰敏。

translations.literal: Conghui took it as a satire on himself and at once punished Min with a large cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Conghui took this as a personal rebuke and immediately forced Min to drink a huge cup of wine as punishment.

sentences.zh: 荊南地狹兵弱，介於吳、楚，為小國。

translations.literal: Jingnan had narrow territory and weak troops, lay between Wu and Chu, and was a small state.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan was a small state with narrow territory and few troops, caught between Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 自吳稱帝，而南漢、閩、楚皆奉梁正朔，歲時貢奉，皆假道荊南。

translations.literal: From the time Wu declared itself emperor, Southern Han, Min, and Chu all observed Liang's calendar and sent seasonal tribute, all passing through Jingnan by courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu declared itself an empire, Southern Han, Min, and Chu still observed Liang's calendar and sent seasonal tribute, all of it routed through Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 季興、從誨常邀留其使者，掠取其物，而諸道以書責誚，或發兵加討，即復還之而無愧。

translations.literal: Jixing and Conghui often detained their envoys and plundered their goods; when the various circuits rebuked them in letters or sent troops to punish them, they would at once return the goods without shame.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing and Conghui often detained envoys and seized their goods. When neighboring circuits rebuked them in writing or sent troops, they would return the goods at once, without a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 其後南漢與閩、蜀皆稱帝，從誨所向稱臣，蓋利其賜予。

translations.literal: Later Southern Han, Min, and Shu all declared themselves emperors; Conghui submitted to whichever he faced, largely for the sake of their gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Southern Han, Min, and Shu all declared themselves emperors, Conghui submitted to whichever court he faced, chiefly for the gifts they bestowed.

sentences.zh: 俚俗語謂奪攘茍得無愧恥者為賴子，猶言無賴也，故諸國皆目為「高賴子」。

translations.literal: In local speech those who seized and snatched without shame were called laizi, meaning rascals; therefore the various states all called them "the Gao rascals."
translations.idiomatic: Local slang called shameless plunderers laizi—rascals—and the neighboring states nicknamed them "the Gao rascals."

sentences.zh: 從誨自求郢州不得，遂自絕於漢。

translations.literal: Since Conghui could not obtain Ying Prefecture when he asked for it, he then cut off relations with Han.
translations.idiomatic: After failing to obtain Ying Prefecture, Conghui broke off relations with Han.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復通朝貢。

translations.literal: After more than a year he resumed court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he resumed tribute and diplomatic contact.

sentences.zh: 乾祐元年十月卒，年五十八，贈尚書令，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth month of the first year of Qianyou, aged fifty-eight; he was posthumously made Director of the Imperial Secretariat; his posthumous title was Literary and Offering.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the first year of Qianyou at the age of fifty-eight. He was posthumously made Director of the Imperial Secretariat with the posthumous title Literary and Offering.

sentences.zh: 子保融立。

translations.literal: His son Baorong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baorong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 從誨十五子，長曰保勛，次保正，保融第三子也，不知其得立之因。

translations.literal: Conghui had fifteen sons; the eldest was Baoqin, the second Baozheng; Baorong was the third son—the reason he came to the throne is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Conghui had fifteen sons: the eldest was Baoqin, the second Baozheng, and Baorong was the third. Why the third son succeeded is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 保融字德長。

translations.literal: Baorong, courtesy name Dechang.
translations.idiomatic: Baorong, whose courtesy name was Dechang.

sentences.zh: 從誨時，為節度副使，兼峽州刺史。

translations.literal: During Conghui's time he was deputy military governor and concurrently prefect of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Conghui he served as deputy military governor and concurrently as prefect of Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從誨卒，拜節度使。

translations.literal: When Conghui died he was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Conghui died he was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年，封渤海郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangshun he was enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangshun he was enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年，進封南平王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiande he was advanced to Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiande he was promoted to Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 世宗征淮，保融遣指揮使魏璘率兵三千，出夏口以為應。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned in Huai, Baorong sent the commander Wei Lin leading three thousand troops out from Xiakou in support.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong campaigned on the Huai, Baorong sent the commander Wei Lin with three thousand men from Xiakou in support.

sentences.zh: 又遣客將劉扶奉箋南唐，勸其內附。

translations.literal: He also sent the guest officer Liu Fu with a memorial to Southern Tang urging it to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent the guest officer Liu Fu with a memorial to Southern Tang urging submission to the central court.

sentences.zh: 李景稱臣，世宗得保融所與箋，大喜，賜以絹百匹。

translations.literal: When Li Jing submitted as a minister, Shizong obtained the memorial Baorong had sent him and was greatly pleased, bestowing a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing submitted, Shizong obtained Baorong's memorial and was delighted, rewarding him with a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 荊南自後唐以來，常數歲一貢京師，而中間兩絕。

translations.literal: Since Later Tang, Jingnan had usually sent tribute to the capital every few years, but twice interrupted the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Since Later Tang, Jingnan had usually sent tribute to the capital every few years, though twice it had broken off entirely.

sentences.zh: 及世宗時，無歲不貢矣。

translations.literal: By Shizong's time there was no year without tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong it sent tribute every year without fail.

sentences.zh: 保融以謂器械金帛，皆土地常產，不足以效誠節，乃遣其弟保紳來朝，世宗益嘉之。

translations.literal: Baorong held that weapons, armor, gold, and silk were all ordinary products of the land and insufficient to show sincerity and loyalty; he therefore sent his younger brother Baoshen to court, and Shizong was all the more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Baorong felt that arms, armor, gold, and silk were merely ordinary local products and insufficient proof of loyalty, so he sent his younger brother Baoshen to court in person. Shizong was still more pleased.

sentences.zh: 初，季興之鎮，梁以兵五千為牙兵，衣食皆給於梁。

translations.literal: At first, when Jixing took the post, Liang supplied five thousand troops as his guard army, and their food and clothing were all provided by Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Jixing first took office, Liang provided five thousand guard troops whose food and clothing were supplied by the Liang court.

sentences.zh: 至明宗時，歲給以鹽萬三千石，後不復給。

translations.literal: By Mingzong's time thirteen thousand piculs of salt were given yearly; later this was no longer supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong the court granted thirteen thousand piculs of salt annually, but later stopped.

sentences.zh: 及世宗平淮，故命泰州給之。

translations.literal: When Shizong pacified Huai, he therefore ordered Taizhou to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong pacified the Huai region, he ordered Taizhou to resume the grant.

sentences.zh: 保勖字省躬，從誨第十子也。

translations.literal: Baoxun, courtesy name Shenggong, was Conghui's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxun, whose courtesy name was Shenggong, was Conghui's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 保融卒，拜節度使。

translations.literal: When Baorong died he was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Baorong died he was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 三年，保勖疾，謂其將梁延嗣曰：「我疾遂不起，兄弟孰可付之後事者？

translations.literal: In the third year Baoxun fell ill and said to his general Liang Yansi: "My illness will surely not lift—which of my brothers can be entrusted with what follows?"
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Baoxun fell gravely ill and asked his general Liang Yansi, "I will not recover. Which of my brothers should inherit command?"

sentences.zh: 」延嗣曰：「公不念貞懿王乎？

translations.literal: Yansi said: "Does Your Lordship not recall Prince Zhenyi?"
translations.idiomatic: Yansi said, "Have you forgotten Prince Zhenyi?"

sentences.zh: 先王寢疾，以軍府付公，今先王子繼沖長矣。

translations.literal: When the former king lay ill he entrusted the military government to Your Lordship; now the former king's son Jichong has come of age.
translations.idiomatic: When the late king lay dying he entrusted the military government to you. His son Jichong is grown now."

sentences.zh: 」保勖曰：「子言是也。

translations.literal: Baoxun said: "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: Baoxun said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 」即以繼沖判內外兵馬。

translations.literal: He thereupon put Jichong in charge of internal and external military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately placed Jichong in charge of all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一月，保勖卒，年三十九，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Baoxun died, aged thirty-nine; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Baoxun died at the age of thirty-nine and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 保融之子繼沖立。

translations.literal: Baorong's son Jichong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Baorong's son Jichong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 繼沖字成和。

translations.literal: Jichong, courtesy name Chenghe.
translations.idiomatic: Jichong, whose courtesy name was Chenghe.

sentences.zh: 保勖卒，拜節度使。

translations.literal: When Baoxun died he was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoxun died he was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 湖南周行逢卒，子保權立，其將張文表作亂，建隆四年，太祖命慕容延釗等討之。

translations.literal: Zhou Xingfeng of Hunan died; his son Baoquan succeeded; his general Zhang Wenbiao rebelled; in the fourth year of Jianlong the Founding Emperor ordered Murong Yanzhao and others to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Xingfeng of Hunan died, his son Baoquan succeeded him, but his general Zhang Wenbiao rebelled. In the fourth year of Jianlong the Founding Emperor ordered Murong Yanzhao and others to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 延釗假道荊南，約以兵過城外。

translations.literal: Yanzhao asked passage through Jingnan, agreeing that his troops would pass outside the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao sought passage through Jingnan on the understanding that his army would march outside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 繼沖大將李景威曰：「兵尚權譎，城外之約，不可信也。

translations.literal: Jichong's great general Li Jingwei said: "Warfare values stratagem and deceit; an agreement to pass outside the walls cannot be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Jichong's chief general Li Jingwei said, "War favors stratagem and deceit. An agreement to pass outside the walls cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 宜嚴兵以待之。

translations.literal: We should array strict troops to await them.
translations.idiomatic: We should mobilize our forces and stand ready."

sentences.zh: 」判官孫光憲叱之曰：「汝峽江一民爾，安識成敗！

translations.literal: The administrative aide Sun Guangxian rebuked him and said: "You are but a commoner of the Gorges and rivers—how would you know success or failure!"
translations.idiomatic: The administrative aide Sun Guangxian rebuked him: "You are nothing but a commoner of the gorges—what do you know of success or failure!"

sentences.zh: 且中國自周世宗時，已有混一天下之志，況聖宋受命，真主出邪！

translations.literal: Moreover the central state, from the time of Emperor Shizong of Zhou, already had the will to unite the realm; how much more now that sacred Song has received the Mandate and the true ruler has appeared!
translations.idiomatic: The central state has sought to unite the realm ever since Emperor Shizong of Zhou. How much more now that sacred Song has received the Mandate and the true ruler has appeared!

sentences.zh: 王師豈易當也！

translations.literal: How easily could imperial troops be resisted!
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops are not to be resisted lightly!"

sentences.zh: 」因勸繼沖去斥候，封府庫以待，繼沖以為然。

translations.literal: He thereupon urged Jichong to remove scouts, seal the treasury and storehouses, and wait; Jichong thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Jichong to withdraw the scouts, seal the treasury, and wait peacefully. Jichong agreed.

sentences.zh: 景威出而嘆曰：「吾言不用，大事去矣，何用生為！

translations.literal: Jingwei went out and sighed: "My words are not used; the great affair is lost—what use is there in living!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingwei left and sighed, "My counsel was ignored. The cause is lost. What point is there in going on!"

sentences.zh: 」因扼吭而死。

translations.literal: He thereupon seized his throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He then strangled himself.

sentences.zh: 延釗軍至，繼沖出逆於郊，而前鋒遽入其城。

translations.literal: When Yanzhao's army arrived, Jichong went out to meet it in the suburbs, but the vanguard suddenly entered his city.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhao's army arrived, Jichong went out to greet it in the suburbs, but the vanguard suddenly entered the city.

sentences.zh: 繼沖亟歸，見旌旗甲馬，布列衢巷，大懼，即詣延釗納牌印，太祖優詔復命繼沖為節度使。

translations.literal: Jichong hurried back, saw banners, flags, armor, and horses arrayed along the streets and lanes, was greatly afraid, and at once went to Yanzhao to surrender his command tally and seal; the Founding Emperor with a gracious edict again appointed Jichong military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Jichong rushed back to find banners, armor, and horses filling every street. Terrified, he went at once to Yanzhao and surrendered his command tally and seal. The Founding Emperor graciously reappointed him military governor.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年，有事於南郊，繼沖上書願陪祠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiande, when rites were performed at the southern suburb, Jichong submitted a memorial wishing to attend the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qiande, when the southern suburban sacrifice was held, Jichong submitted a memorial asking to take part.

sentences.zh: 九月，具文告三廟，率其將吏宗族五百餘人朝於京師，拜武寧軍節度使以卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he prepared written announcements to the three ancestral temples, led more than five hundred of his generals, officials, and clansmen to court in the capital, was appointed military governor of the Wuning Army, and there died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he made written offerings at the three ancestral temples, led more than five hundred generals, officials, and kinsmen to court in the capital, was appointed military governor of the Wuning Army, and died there.

sentences.zh: 光憲拜黃州刺史，其後事具國史。

translations.literal: Guangxian was appointed prefect of Huang Prefecture; his later affairs are recorded in full in the dynastic history.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxian was appointed prefect of Huang Prefecture. His later career is recorded in the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: （季興興滅年世甚明，諸書皆同，蓋自梁開平元年鎮荊南，至皇朝乾德元年國除，凡五十七年。）〉

translations.literal: (The rise and fall of Jixing's house are very clear in the dates; all books agree: from the first year of Kaiping of Liang when he governed Jingnan, to the first year of Qiande of the imperial dynasty when the state was abolished—in all fifty-seven years.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Accounts of Gao Jixing's rise and fall agree across sources: from Liang Kaiping 1 [907], when he took Jingnan, until our dynasty's Qiande 1 [963], when the state was abolished—a total of fifty-seven years.)〉
